## Hinge question · Which observations are in the middle? {#l2-hinge .compact .median-table-hinge}

| $x$ | $f$ | $fx$ | $cf$ | $rf$ | $crf$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 2 | 3 | 6 | 3 | 0.15 | 0.15 |
| 4 | 7 | 28 | 10 | 0.35 | 0.50 |
| 7 | 6 | 42 | 16 | 0.30 | 0.80 |
| 9 | 3 | 27 | 19 | 0.15 | 0.95 |
| 12 | 1 | 12 | 20 | 0.05 | 1.00 |
| **Total** | **20** | **115** | — | **1.00** | — |

<p class="column-key"><span data-math="cf">cf</span>: cumulative frequency · <span data-math="rf">rf</span>: relative frequency · <span data-math="crf">crf</span>: cumulative relative frequency</p>

```{=html}
<div data-module="hinge" data-correct="2" class="hinge numeric-choices">
<p class="hinge-question">What is the median? Use the table to justify your answer.</p>
<div class="hinge-toolbar"><div class="time" role="timer" aria-label="Time remaining">1:00</div><div class="toolbar"><label>Seconds <select class="timer-duration" aria-label="Question duration"><option>30</option><option>45</option><option selected>60</option><option>90</option><option>120</option></select></label><button class="timer-start primary">Start</button><button class="reset-question">Reset</button></div></div>
<div class="choices"><button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span>4</span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span>5.5</span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span>7</span></button><button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span>10.5</span></button></div>
<div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly. On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button></div>
<div class="hinge-explanation" hidden>2. The 10th observation is 4 and the 11th is 7, so the median is <span data-math="\frac{4+7}{2}=5.5">(4 + 7)/2 = 5.5</span>.</div>
</div>
```

::: notes
All six columns are deliberately complete: x, f, fx, cf, rf and crf. Students must choose relevant information and interpret the cumulative boundary. No further table calculations are needed. n=20; Σfx=115; the mean would be5.75, but the question asks for the median.

Allow60 seconds; students think independently with fists on chests. On “show”, collect simultaneous1–4 finger responses before revealing. Correct answer2: positions10 and11 contain4 and7. A median need not appear among the observed values.

- Choice1 (4): takes only the10th observation, or confuses the mode with the median; cf=10/crf=.50 is the end of the row, not the whole median calculation.
- Choice2 (5.5): correctly averages the two middle data values.
- Choice3 (7): takes only the11th observation or the middle of the five distinct x-values, ignoring frequencies.
- Choice4 (10.5): reports the average position rather than the data value.

Ready: ask why crf=.50 atx=4 does not make the median4, or ask for the mean and contrast its calculation.
Divided: ask students to name the10th and11th observations separately, then re-poll.
Reteach: label row positions1–3,4–10,11–16,17–19,20; locate both middle values, then re-poll.
:::
